findings.text: Akşamın azalan görünürlüğü ile ağlama gösterisi birleşerek denetlenebilir kanıtın yerine duygusal sesi geçirmeye çalışan bir sahne kurar.

activation_trace.role: Ordinary coming supplies the movement that culminates before the father.
Fatherhood and nurture make the addressee the scene's receiving and protective authority.
The evening-time image fixes the arrival at the late-day and night threshold.
Sorrow, tears, and voice supply the manifest affect carried into the encounter.

changed_reading.after: Their return is an affective appeal delivered to the household's paternal protector at a vulnerable night threshold.
changed_reading.before: They came home at night while crying.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction joins جاءوا, أباهم, عشاء, and يبكون as movement, recipient, time, and manifest affect.
baseline_models.mechanism: A collective movement terminates at the father-as-caregiver after nightfall, with crying supplying sorrow, tears, or voice; the event is an appeal for paternal reception rather than bare locomotion.

activation_trace.role: Night darkness and low clarity supply reduced inspectability as the display's condition.
Affected weeping supplies the exploratory possibility of performed rather than spontaneous grief.
The nurturing father is the intended evaluator and emotional audience of the surface.

changed_reading.after: Evening can function as reduced inspectability while possibly affected crying becomes an emotionally legible surface offered to the father; this remains a possibility, not an assertion.
changed_reading.before: Evening is an incidental timestamp and the crying transparently reports grief.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: عشاء stands beside يبكون, and the display is directed to أباهم.
baseline_models.mechanism: Reduced nocturnal visibility lets audible or visible grief dominate what the father can assess. The form-distant affected-weeping branch keeps open, without asserting, the possibility that the group presents a managed emotional surface.

activation_trace.role: Low clarity makes the focus scene an apt site for ambiguous evidence.
Tears, sorrow, and voice provide the immediately visible or audible sign to be assessed.
The manifest-sign image casts the focus affect as something legible but not automatically self-interpreting.
Disclosure by speech or sign supplies the criterion against which the dark emotional display is tested.
Reason as a restraint on ignorance supplies the reader's check against immediate affective assent.
Following a trace makes sequential comparison, rather than isolated appearance, the disclosure mechanism.

changed_reading.after: The crying is an ambiguous sign whose value emerges only when its dark presentation is traced against the surrounding sequence.
changed_reading.before: The crying is a transparent report of the group's inner grief.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening frame turns the focus display into an evidentiary problem: a visible sign under low visibility must be disclosed by restrained reasoning and by following the sequence, so tears cannot authenticate themselves in isolation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies visible-sign, disclosure, reason-as-restraint, and trace-following images; I infer that the tears should be read as evidence within a sequence rather than accepted alone. Alternatively, the opening frame may guide the reader globally without making these tears locally suspect.
structural_cues: 12:1-3 frame the pericope as manifest signs made intelligible through a sequentially told account.
The focus presents affect under darkness before later claims and objects can be checked.

activation_trace.role: Spoken utterance establishes the earlier child-to-father disclosure channel.
Direct father-address marks the earlier report as an intimate paternal communication.
The dream-vision image supplies the content of the first disclosure that the later scene competes with.
The packet's split narration image makes the vision also a transmitted report, sharpening the parallel with the brothers' report.
Stratagem and contrivance supply the mechanism by which a rival disclosure could be engineered.
The same paternal authority becomes the recipient whose prior understanding is at stake.
Possibly affected weeping supplies a nonverbal counter-report, with its form distance keeping the claim exploratory.

changed_reading.after: Their crying arrival can operate as a counter-revelation, trying to replace Joseph's earlier vision with the group's emotionally staged version of events.
changed_reading.before: The brothers merely report a new calamity to their father.

context_deltas.mechanism: Joseph's singular dream disclosure to his father is followed by a warning about sibling stratagem; the brothers' plural, affect-laden return to the same father can therefore function as a rival disclosure intended to overwrite the father's prior visual and narrative frame.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies dream, report, paternal address, stratagem, and possible affected weeping; I infer that the group display competes with the earlier disclosure for control of the father's reading. Alternatively, the two encounters may be parallel without the later one deliberately answering the first.
structural_cues: 12:4 is a singular son-to-father disclosure, whereas 12:16 is a plural group-to-father display.
12:5 explicitly places sibling stratagem between the two paternal encounters.

activation_trace.role: Love lodged in the heart supplies the scarce paternal attachment over which the brothers compete.
Fatherhood and nurture locate the rivalry inside a relation of care.
A surrounding, mutually supporting group supplies the coordinated social body that returns crying.
The father's face and forward attention supply the object the group seeks to clear for itself.
Collective coming delivers the rival group back into the father's presence.
Affected weeping supplies the possible instrument for capturing sympathy and paternal attention.

changed_reading.after: The group may use grief to reoccupy the paternal attention it complained was withheld, making the return a social seizure as well as a report.
changed_reading.before: The group seeks paternal comfort after suffering a loss.

context_deltas.mechanism: The group names unequal paternal love, identifies itself as a mutually supporting band, and imagines the father's face becoming available after Joseph's removal. Its collective crying return can thus be a bid to occupy the paternal attention whose distribution generated the plot.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies rivalry for love, cohesive group force, the father's face, and possible affected crying; I infer that grief can function as coordinated affective occupation after the rival's removal. Alternatively, guilt or fear could produce unplanned tears even within the same rivalry.
structural_cues: 12:8 names both the love asymmetry and the brothers' group identity.
12:9 makes exclusive access to the father's face an explicit desired outcome.

activation_trace.role: Security and settled trust supply the relational credit the brothers obtained before departure.
Purity from fraud supplies the claimed quality of their counsel and intention.
Guarding and watchful care supply the concrete duty the return scene must account for.
Manifest sorrow supplies an emotional substitute for the absent protected person and failed custody.
The father as guardian and nurturer is the creditor to whom the failed pledge must be answered.

changed_reading.after: The tears also act as affective collateral, offered where promised guardianship and fraud-free counsel have failed.
changed_reading.before: The tears simply register the loss they have come to announce.

context_deltas.mechanism: Before departure the brothers solicit trust, claim freedom from adulteration, and promise guardianship. When they return without the protected person, crying can function as affective collateral offered in place of the trust, purity, and custody their earlier words pledged.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies trust, unadulterated counsel, guardianship, absence, and crying; I infer that tears replace the missing performance of the pledge with affective evidence. Alternatively, genuinely failed guardians could offer the same tears without strategic substitution.
structural_cues: 12:11-12 place trust, pure counsel, and an explicit protection claim before the departure.
12:16 reverses that movement: the guardians return to the father while the guarded son does not.

activation_trace.role: The roughening of the self by grief supplies the affective register first voiced by the father.
Fear as expectation of harm supplies the father's advance scenario rather than a later discovery.
The prey image gives the feared event its victim-predator mechanism.
Wolfish predation supplies the exact agent image later adopted by the brothers.
Leaving something outside vigilance supplies the lapse built into the father's forecast.
The mutually supporting group image makes the brothers' adoption of the scenario a collective performance.
Affected weeping supplies the possible enactment of the father's preannounced grief.

changed_reading.after: Their crying can be borrowed affect: they perform the father's already voiced grief so that his own feared wolf scenario arrives feeling emotionally confirmed.
changed_reading.before: The brothers cry because the alleged wolf attack has made them grieve.

context_deltas.mechanism: The father supplies both the anticipated affect and the feared causal scenario: grief at separation, dread of predation, and the group's inattention. The group then repeats the predator scenario, so its crying can perform the father's own forecasted grief back to him before the verbal account.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a preannounced grief, expected harm, predator script, vigilance lapse, group response, and possible affected crying; I infer that the brothers borrow the father's affect to make his fear feel fulfilled. Alternatively, witnesses to a feared event might naturally mirror the fearer's emotional language.
structural_cues: 12:13 gives the father both the grief and wolf scenario before the brothers claim it.
12:14 rehearses their answer, and 12:16 places crying before their detailed account.

activation_trace.role: Resolved gathering of opinion supplies the unified agency behind the concealment and return.
Making something assume a condition supplies the deliberate transfer of Joseph into hiddenness.
A depression in which something disappears supplies the spatial image of removed visibility.
The cut, unlined well gives the concealment a bounded downward container.
Fine awareness and subtle perception supply the epistemic capacity explicitly absent around the concealment.
Night darkness extends the pit's reduced visibility into the paternal encounter.
Audible or visible grief becomes the substitute presence offered where Joseph is no longer visible.

changed_reading.after: Their evening arrival transports the pit's hiddenness into the father's field of perception, replacing the unseen son with an intensely perceptible display.
changed_reading.before: The brothers happen to reach home in the evening after leaving Joseph behind.

context_deltas.mechanism: A resolved collective makes Joseph disappear into the pit's hidden depth while fine perception is absent. The next movement carries that hiddenness into the father's world: evening lowers visibility, and crying supplies a perceptible substitute for the son who has been placed beyond sight.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies collective resolve, deliberate placement, a disappearing depth, a well, absent fine awareness, night darkness, and crying; I infer a transfer of hiddenness from pit to household, with affect replacing the hidden body. Alternatively, evening may be only chronological and not spatially analogous to the pit.
structural_cues: 12:15 places Joseph below sight; 12:16 immediately moves the brothers toward the father under evening darkness.
The concealed son is absent from the return, but the brothers' affect is emphatically present.

activation_trace.role: Possibly affected weeping supplies the package's pre-verbal emotional layer.
Saying what was not supplies the false proposition that follows the tears.
Heart-settling belief supplies the response the speakers explicitly predict they will not obtain.
Truthful speech supplies the standard they invoke while staging a claim that fails it.
Bringing and presenting something turns the repeated coming into delivery of a material exhibit.
The worn shirt supplies the physical surface on which the claim is staged.
Recognizable blood supplies the bodily index meant to certify injury and death.
A garment that lies by its condition precisely exposes the shirt as a deceptive material statement.

changed_reading.after: The focus is the opening layer of a multimodal proof package: performed grief prepares a doubtful claim, and the claim is then embodied in a garment that lies by its condition.
changed_reading.before: The brothers arrive crying and later add corroborating evidence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The tears precede speech; the speech anticipates disbelief; the repeated coming then extends into bringing a shirt marked with false blood. Performance, proposition, and object form a layered credibility package, while the lying-garment branch exposes the material exhibit as another expressive surface.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the affect-speech-object sequence, anticipated unbelief, repeated coming, recognizable blood, and a lying garment; I infer an ordered persuasion strategy in which each layer supports the next. Alternatively, the tears could be spontaneous even though the proposition and object are false.
structural_cues: 12:16 ends with weeping; 12:17 supplies the claim and anticipates disbelief; 12:18 repeats coming and presents the shirt with false blood.
The father's response rejects the package as an internally embellished account rather than accepting any layer alone.

remaining_uncertainties: يبكون itself does not morphologically require affected crying; that activation depends on a form-distant branch and contextual fit.
عشاء may remain a simple time reference even though low visibility and transferred hiddenness form a coherent mechanism.
The split ر ء ي to ر و ي and د م و to د م ي mappings generate diagnostic outliers but remain deliberately exploratory.
strongest_changes: Evening changed from a timestamp into a condition of reduced inspectability in which affect must be audited as a sign.
Crying changed from transparent grief into coordinated affect shaped by rivalry, broken pledges, and the father's own preannounced fear.
The 12:16-18 sequence changed the arrival into a layered proof package of tears, doubtful speech, and a garment that lies by its condition.
summary.what_was_special: Several readings remain live together: a paternal grief appeal, strategic affective occupation, transfer of the pit's hiddenness, and exploratory fluid or counter-narrative images. The context intensifies suspicion without making every lexical branch collapse into one final interpretation.

activation_trace.role: Collected wound discharge supplies the strange material image that fluidizes the group's coming.
Tears within crying supply the first plausible bodily fluid in the display.
Bleeding and a bloody wound supply the second fluid sign and complete the wound-like presentation.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the arrival carries a manufactured wound-fluid register: tear-flow prepares the bloody sign as though the group itself were presenting an injury.
changed_reading.before: The verse reports people moving while they cry.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the remote wound-discharge image of ج ي ء rather than ordinary coming. It remains anchored by جاءوا, tear-capable يبكون, and the next-ayah bleeding image, but downstream prose should label it a material analogy among fluids, not a lexical derivation or literal claim about the verb.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: جاءوا and يبكون place coming beside a potentially flowing bodily sign, immediately before the blood exhibit.

activation_trace.role: The split root's narration image turns the earlier vision into a reportable account against which another account can compete.
Rivalry and prevailing in weeping supply the strange image of a group competing through affective narration.
The split root's depicted-image branch makes the blood stain function like a constructed picture of the alleged event.
The lying-garment image turns that constructed picture into a material counter-story.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the brothers mount a competitive counter-narration to Joseph's earlier vision, using weeping and a pictorially staged garment to install their own image of events.
changed_reading.before: Crying accompanies a spoken report that is supported by a stained shirt.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it combines packet-resolved non-dominant mappings with the form-distant competitive-weeping branch. It remains anchored in the earlier vision-report, the focus crying before the same father, and the next-ayah depicted blood and lying garment; downstream prose should render it as a cross-domain counter-narration, not as morphology required by the surface forms.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The group comes crying to the father who earlier received Joseph's vision-report, then supports its account with a staged garment.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Dim time and manufactured tears cooperate as evidentiary cover.** ع ش و B004/B001 (evening; dim clarity) and ب ك ي B004 (forced or feigned crying) are structurally compressed into one short arrival scene. I infer that reduced visibility helps performance substitute for inspectable fact. The ayah reads as staging: time, affect, and approach are coordinated.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:18 shifted verification from dim affective performance to the visible shirt, correcting tears with material evidence.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Weeping used as evidential sound.** The variants under `ب ك ي:B001` jointly specify grief, tears, and vocal lament. The terse ayah supplies crying before the brothers state their claim in 12:17, while 12:18 supplies the manufactured blood and the father rejects their description. The packet gives affect first and evidence second; I infer that the display is meant to pre-load the report with credibility. *Yabkūn* therefore reads as a performed evidential channel whose sound cannot establish the event asserted.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:84-86 distinguishes Jacob's embodied grief and directed complaint from this performed weeping, showing retrospectively that tears acquire evidentiary value only through their relation to truthful disclosure.

words.gloss_range: opening connector that can resume or coordinate the narrated return; it links without spelling out motive
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as a connected return, not as an isolated scene. The connector can be heard as resumption or coordination, so the prose should keep the boundary alive: the concealed well-scene has moved into public arrival, but the particle itself does not explain the brothers' motive. Because it is fused to {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}), the transition is visually and audibly carried straight into the arrival verb.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the following arrival verb to which the opening connector is attached

topics.headline: connected scene launch without fixed motive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by carrying the prior concealment into a new public return while leaving the exact discourse force and motive unstated.
topics.reason: QAC allows either coordinating or resumptive force for the opening connector, so the exclusive labels must be narrowed to a connected boundary function rather than one fixed subtype.

topics.headline: fused connector carries arrival forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the one-letter connector is not detached from the action; it is graphically and recitationally joined to the arrival.
topics.reason: The particle is a proclitic attached to the following verb, preserving the source row's visual and audible continuity payoff.

words.gloss_range: they came or arrived before their father, with the narrative pressure of presentation kept secondary
words.prose: {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) makes the brothers appear only as a plural verb ending: the group arrives, but no individual is named. Its perfect form completes the motion before the ongoing weeping of {{ar:يَبْكُونَ}} ({{tr:yabkūna}}), so the ayah moves from a bounded entrance to a prolonged display. The local sequence starts with arrival, then gives the father, then nightfall, then tears, setting up the spoken claim in the next ayah (12:17). The local syntax gives {{ar:أَبَاهُمْ}} ({{tr:abāhum}}) as the reached father, so any 'bringing' or 'presenting' sense must stay as narrative shadow: the fabricated account and shirt are not a separate local object in this word. The long ā and medial hamza make the sound catch before the plural ending, fitting arrival as motion that stops in presence. Within Surah 12, this first deceptive arrival before the father looks ahead to answering arrivals and restorations (12:93-96; 12:100).
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arrival, reaching presence, and event-emergence; local grammar selects completed plural arrival before a relational endpoint

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the father reached by the arrival verb
the circumstantial weeping clause that follows the completed arrival

topics.headline: unnamed plural arrival as completed public action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers become a collective grammatical action rather than named individuals, and that their arrival is complete before the tears continue.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect 3mp with pro-drop subject agreement, and the following imperfect circumstantial clause supports the completed-arrival versus ongoing-weeping contrast.

topics.headline: arrival selected while presentation remains a narrative shadow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the motion toward the father doubles as the delivery of a staged account, while the local parse still treats the father as the explicit reached endpoint.
topics.reason: Rows that speak of a suppressed brought-object are narrowed because attachment evidence marks {{ar:أَبَاهُمْ}} ({{tr:abāhum}}) as the explicit object reached by the verb; the presentation payoff survives only as narrative pressure.

topics.headline: deceptive coming answered by later arrivals
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this arrival is the negative pole of later Surah 12 arrival scenes where the family route and shirt motif are morally reversed (12:93-96; 12:100).
topics.reason: The source rows give concrete same-surah and cross-surah references; they are preserved as echo and contrast, not as controls on the local parse.

topics.headline: arrival sets recipient, time, manner, then speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb starts a staged sequence: arrival first, father next, nightfall and tears after, and only then the spoken claim in the following ayah (12:17).
topics.reason: The local word order and the next-ayah reference support the staged movement without adding a new lexical sense.

topics.headline: glottal catch fits completed arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sound-shape of the arrival word catches before the plural ending, matching motion that comes to a stop in presence.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is local to the surface form and does not conflict with the grammar.

words.gloss_range: their father, the immediate relational recipient of the brothers' arrival
words.prose: {{ar:أَبَاهُمْ}} ({{tr:abāhum}}) makes the father definite through the brothers' own suffix: he is not introduced by name, but as their father. The noun-five accusative shape, with its long ā case-marking, makes him the reached endpoint of {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}), and the suffix binds the unnamed plural subject to the person they are about to deceive. The broader father/ancestor range is narrowed here to the immediate household relation, while still letting the father stand as the vulnerable origin-point to which the sons return. Later Surah 12 scenes answer this deceived father-position with restored parental honor (12:100).
words.root_gloss_range: father, paternal source, ancestor, or household origin; local suffix and singular form select the immediate father rather than an ancestral plural

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the arrival verb that reaches the father as endpoint

topics.headline: their father is defined through the brothers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the father enters the scene relationally, through the same unnamed plural group that has been carrying the action.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix is syntactically forced and resolves to the brothers, so the relational definiteness and pronoun-chain payoff are locally secure.

topics.headline: case marks the father as reached recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the father is placed immediately after the arrival verb as the person reached before the time and weeping details are added.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the noun-five accusative form and attachment evidence marks the father as the explicit object or endpoint of the arrival.

topics.headline: immediate father, not ancestral abstraction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a broad fatherhood and origin field is compressed into one household encounter with a specific deceived father.
topics.reason: The broad father, ancestor, and source claims are narrowed because the local singular possessive form selects the immediate father; V4 has no root entry here to license additional branch expansion.

topics.headline: deceived father-position answered later
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this father-directed deception belongs to a larger Surah 12 father-relation network that later turns toward honor and restoration (12:100).
topics.reason: The rows supply concrete same-surah father references, so the echo survives as a relational arc rather than as a new local lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: at evening or nightfall, as an indefinite accusative time adverb
words.prose: {{ar:عِشَاءًۭ}} ({{tr:ʿishāʾan}}) is not a decorative timestamp. As an indefinite accusative time adverb, it folds the evening hour directly into the arrival without a preposition and carries the ayah's only explicit timing, making this rare adverbial deployment structurally exposed. The selected sense is evening or nightfall, but the {{ar:ع ش و}} ({{tr:ʿ-sh-w}}) field also includes dimness and weak night-sight, so the father's reception is staged under constrained seeing. Its canonical extended form lets the evening word linger and then catch at the hamza before the ayah moves into weeping. The evening side also stands alone here, without the morning counterpart of morning-evening formulae (19:11; 19:62).
